title: Multi-Digit Multiplication
description: Learn multi-digit multiplication for Class 4 Maths — multiply 4-digit by 1-digit, 2-digit by 2-digit using column method and area model. Includes estimation, solved examples, 10 MCQs and 6 IMO questions.

topics.title: Multiply 4-Digit by 1-Digit
topics.concept:
Multiplying a 4-digit number by a 1-digit number means repeated addition. We use the column method (standard algorithm) with carrying.

Steps:

  • Align numbers by the rightmost digit
  • Multiply each digit from right to left
  • If the product has two digits, write the units digit and carry the tens digit
  • Add the carry to the next multiplication

Example: 4,523 x 4 = 18,092
topics.visual: <svg viewBox='0 0 480 160' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' style='max-width:100%;font-family:sans-serif'><rect width='480' height='160' fill='#fffbeb' rx='8'/><text stroke="none" x='240' y='20' font-size='13' font-weight='bold' fill='#92400e' text-anchor='middle'>Column Multiplication: 4,523 x 4</text><text stroke="none" x='180' y='50' font-size='14' fill='#374151' text-anchor='end'>4,523</text><text stroke="none" x='190' y='50' font-size='14' fill='#374151'>x   4</text><line x1='80' y1='58' x2='220' y2='58' stroke='#374151' stroke-width='1.5'/><text stroke="none" x='60' y='78' font-size='11' fill='#dc2626'>Ones: 4x3=12 write 2, carry 1</text><text stroke="none" x='60' y='96' font-size='11' fill='#059669'>Tens: 4x2=8 + 1(carry) = 9</text><text stroke="none" x='60' y='114' font-size='11' fill='#1d4ed8'>Hundreds: 4x5=20 write 0, carry 2</text><text stroke="none" x='60' y='132' font-size='11' fill='#7c3aed'>Thousands: 4x4=16 + 2(carry) = 18</text><text stroke="none" x='400' y='85' font-size='22' font-weight='bold' fill='#b45309' text-anchor='middle'>18,092</text></svg>

examples.solution: Step 1: 4x3=12, write 2 carry 1. Step 2: 4x2=8+1=9, write 9. Step 3: 4x5=20, write 0 carry 2. Step 4: 4x4=16+2=18, write 18. Answer: 18,092.
Step 1: 8x8=64, write 4 carry 6. Step 2: 8x6=48+6=54, write 4 carry 5. Step 3: 8x0=0+5=5, write 5. Step 4: 8x7=56, write 56. Answer: 56,544.

examples.problem: A stadium has 2,456 seats. Each ticket costs Rs.9. What is the total collection for a full house?
examples.solution: Multiply 2,456 x 9. 9x6=54 (write 4, carry 5). 9x5=45+5=50 (write 0, carry 5). 9x4=36+5=41 (write 1, carry 4). 9x2=18+4=22. Answer: Rs.22,104.

recap: Align numbers so the rightmost digits line up
Multiply from right to left — ones, tens, hundreds, thousands
When product has two digits, write units and carry tens to next column
Always add the carry before writing the final digit

topics.title: Multiply 2-Digit by 2-Digit (Area Model)
topics.concept:
When multiplying by a 2-digit number, we split it into two parts and multiply separately, then add the partial products.

Area Model: Break both numbers into tens and ones, then multiply each part.

Example: 23 x 45 = (20+3) x (40+5) = 800 + 100 + 120 + 15 = 1,035

Column Method:

  • Multiply by the ones digit first
  • Then multiply by the tens digit (add a placeholder zero)
  • Add both partial products

topics.title: Estimate Products Before Calculating
topics.concept:
Estimation helps us check if our answer is reasonable. We round numbers to a convenient value before multiplying.

How to Estimate:

  • Round each number to the nearest 10, 100, or 1,000
  • Multiply the rounded numbers
  • Compare with the actual answer — they should be close

Estimation is especially useful to detect calculation errors!

examples.problem: Estimate and then find the actual product of 487 x 32.
examples.solution: Estimate: 487 rounds to 500; 32 rounds to 30. Estimate = 500 x 30 = 15,000. Actual: 487 x 32 = 15,584. The estimate (15,000) is close to the actual (15,584).
Round 2,345 to 2,000. Estimate = 2,000 x 7 = 14,000. Or round to 2,300: 2,300 x 7 = 16,100. Actual: 2,345 x 7 = 16,415. Both estimates are in the right range.

examples.problem: A farmer harvests 1,236 kg of wheat per day. Estimate how much he harvests in a week (7 days).
examples.solution: Round 1,236 to 1,200. Estimate = 1,200 x 7 = 8,400 kg. Actual: 1,236 x 7 = 8,652 kg. The estimate (8,400) is a good approximation.

recap: Round numbers to the nearest 10, 100 or 1,000 before estimating
Estimation catches big errors in your calculations
The actual answer should be close to the estimated answer
Useful in real life when exact calculations are not needed
